hints: Put the two tangent terms over the denominator $1-\tan^2\theta$.
Factor out $\tan\theta$ and simplify the remaining ratio.
Convert that ratio using the double-angle cosine identity to obtain $\sec2\theta$.
walkthrough:
Apply the double angle formula for tangent $\tan 2\theta = \dfrac{2\tan\theta}{1 - \tan^2\theta}$ to the left-hand side:
$$\tan 2\theta - \tan\theta = \dfrac{2\tan\theta}{1 - \tan^2\theta} - \tan\theta$$

Use the Pythagorean identity $1 + \tan^2\theta = \sec^2\theta$ and the double angle identity $\cos 2\theta = \dfrac{1 - \tan^2\theta}{1 + \tan^2\theta}$ which gives $\sec 2\theta = \dfrac{1 + \tan^2\theta}{1 - \tan^2\theta}$:
$$= \tan\theta \cdot \dfrac{1 + \tan^2\theta}{1 - \tan^2\theta} = \tan\theta\sec 2\theta$$
This matches the right-hand side, completing the proof.

ai_rubric.Trigonometric Identities: Applies $\tan2A$ formula to express LHS in terms of $\tan\theta$; Applies Pythagoras or $\cos2A$ formula; Concludes with $\tan2\theta-\tan\theta\equiv\tan\theta\sec2\theta$.

hints: Replace the integrand by $\tan2\theta-\tan\theta$ using part (i).
Integrate each tangent term as a logarithm of cosine, accounting for the factor 2 in $2\theta$.
Use exact cosine values and the quotient law for logarithms to show the claimed result.
walkthrough:
Use the identity from part (i) to rewrite the integrand:
$$\int_0^{\pi/6} \tan\theta\sec 2\theta\,\mathrm{d}\theta = \int_0^{\pi/6} (\tan 2\theta - \tan\theta)\,\mathrm{d}\theta$$

Subtract the lower limit evaluation from the upper limit evaluation:
$$\int_0^{\pi/6} \tan\theta\sec 2\theta\,\mathrm{d}\theta = \dfrac{1}{2}\ln\left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right) - 0 = \dfrac{1}{2}\ln\left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right)$$

ai_rubric.Integration: Integrates and derives a term of the form $a\ln(\cos2\theta)$ or $b\ln(\cos\theta)$ (or secant equivalents); Derives integral $-\frac12\ln(\cos2\theta)+\ln(\cos\theta)$, or equivalent; Concludes with $\displaystyle\int_0^{\frac16\pi}\tan\theta\sec2\theta\,d\theta=\frac12\ln\frac32$.
